chunks: What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū Saʿīd al-Mukārī, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Madhy comes out from a man.” He said: “Shall I set for you a criterion regarding it?” He said: I said: “Yes, may I be made your ransom.” He said: “If it comes out from you with desire, then perform wudu (ablution); and if it comes out from you in other than that manner, then there is no wudu (ablution) upon you because of it.”

key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid discussed in the ruling
key_terms.شَهْوَةٍ: sexual desire, which determines the legal ruling here
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: ritual ablution required before acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about madhy and whether it necessitates wudu (ablution). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام sets a criterion based on whether the discharge occurs with desire, making this narration relevant to rulings of ritual purity.
